??? quote "Dialogue"

    - Zip! Zip Calloway. Nobody calls me Zinnia except when I am in trouble, which is often, so you might hear it. I am going to be famous. I have a head start: I already broke an arm.
    - Not wasted! I wrote it on my wall. And the bill part, too, smaller, underneath. I argue with it every morning. It wins.
    - I brought the lamp back! In one piece! Margo checked it three ways and then hugged it. Then me. In that order.
    - You. Did. It. Without me. I am furious. I am also so happy I could fall off a bank. Tell me again. The size of it. The noise.
    - Second day, *Player*! That is what we train on now. You walk away, and you come back when it is yours. Torvi says I am getting it. Torvi said it twice.
    - What do you want to know? Ask me anything. Ask me about the arm.
        - *Choice:* Tell me about your arm.
        - *Choice:* What is Torvi teaching you?
        - *Choice:* Margo's spark lamp?
        - *Choice:* Nothing. Goodbye.
    - Last spring, a caravan to Kaldemor, two days out. A monster burst out of the brush. Huge. Bigger than a wagon. Bigger than two wagons. Eyes like lanterns. Tusks like, like scythes!
    - And I charged it. Alone. Across a raging river and up a cliff, and I nearly had it, and then the cliff gave way. Arm in two places. Tick has three versions in his book. This one is the best. Do not ask Torvi.
    - Something big came out of the brush, and I ran at it with a borrowed sword, and it was gone, and I fell off a bank onto a rock. That is it. Version four. It is shorter. Tick likes it best. I am starting to as well.
    - Torvi carried me back to the wagons over one shoulder while I was still shouting about tusks. Then laughed at me. Then, back here, I followed Torvi round the Gate Walk until Torvi gave in.
    - Every morning, the open ground inside the gate. Footwork, guard, when to stand. And when to run. That one I hate. My feet only know forwards.
    - Margo built a lamp that throws sparks to scare monsters off the roads! Bolt tested it on a broom, a barrel and himself. I volunteered before she finished asking. I promised to bring it back. I will. Probably. Definitely.
    - It works! On ordinary boar, anyway. Sparks, bang, and off they go squealing. I brought it back, like I promised. Margo says I am her favourite tester. Bolt says that is not fair.
    - Bye! If anyone dares you to do anything, send them to me.
